notes: ACCESS: direct fetch worked for every page throughout, no WAF/blocking encountered (HTTP 200 on all URLs below). RULE 3 SANITY CHECK PASSED: Organization JSON-LD confirms 'Connox', HQ phone +49 511 166 53352 (Hannover, Germany, matches the known real Connox HQ), live Impressum/imprint and legal pages, established design retailer since ~2004, no liquidation/closing-down banner language anywhere. Genuine live company, not a scam domain. STRUCTURE: built from the full mega-menu (400 nav links crawled) plus verification fetches of grouping-hub pages (accessories/home-decor/design-mirror.html, accessories/wall-decorations.html, accessories/candles-candle-holder.html, accessories/table-decoration.html) which have NO own product-list-react section (pure hubs) - their linked children were used as the leaf rows instead of the hub itself. QTY: Connox category pages are 100% client-side rendered - the static HTML/CDN response contains only an empty '<section id="products" class="product-list-react">' mount point with no product tiles or count text; confirmed with direct fetch, a Googlebot user-agent (no server-side prerender differentiation), and WebFetch (which also only sees the unrendered shell). Reverse-engineered the app bundles (connox.124.min.js, cnxwp.124.min.js, productlist.js) to find the underlying data API (https://api.connox.io/v1/shop/100005/items, shopId confirmed via document.body data-channel=100005). The endpoint is live and does return real data for a direct itemIds lookup (verified against a known product, itemId=117762, which returned full price/attribute/category JSON), and it DOES validate input (an invalid view= param throws a proper INVALID_VIEW_PARAMETER error) - but every attempted category-browse query (categoryId, subCategoryId, mainCategoryId, categoryIds tried against the item's own categoryId=106495, its subCategoryIds=[100228], and the page's CMS ProductSubCategoryId=100228, across multiple shopIds and curl_cffi browser-impersonation profiles) returns an empty result set with no error, and the productlist.js UI chunk contains zero references to categoryId/itemContent/totalSearchHits - the real category-browse call is evidently issued by a further lazy-loaded chunk never fetched by a non-executing HTTP client. As a fallback, cross-checked a sitemap URL-prefix enumeration (8 sitemap files, 14,580 URLs total) but found it provably unreliable as a qty proxy: e.g. the nav's 'Candlestick' listing page (home-decor/candle-holders.html) has only 24 product URLs filed under its own path, while a disjoint set of 206 clearly-related candlestick products is filed under a completely different path (accessories/home-decor/candlestick/) - proving products are cross-listed into category pages via internal category IDs, not reliably filed under the URL folder of the page that lists them, so a sitemap-prefix count cannot be trusted as exact either (same failure mode as Rule 1's href-counting trap, one level up). Per Rule 1/THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS, qty is therefore null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag on every leaf row rather than an unverified number; every link below was independently verified live (HTTP 200) and, where spot-checked, breadcrumb-confirmed to the stated category (e.g. Pendant Luminaires product page breadcrumb: Home > Categories > Lighting > Pendant luminaires). RULE 0 GAINS: included Outdoor Lighting (a location/room branch, would have been skipped under old room-exclusion habits), and Standing Mirrors / Cosmetic Mirrors (floor and vanity/makeup mirror types, Rule 0.3). EXCLUDED: light bulbs (lighting/bulbs.html), Scented Candles (accessories/home-decor/scented-candles.html, explicit Home Fragrance exclusion), the general 'Candles' node (home-decor/candles.html) - excluded under the standing default caution for unverifiable scented/unscented product mix since the listing cannot be rendered to inspect titles; Pinboards (functional office/organisation item, not decor); Tapestries (site's own Home Textiles taxonomy, fabric wall-hangings, excluded per textiles default); the 'design mobiles' node (nursery/kids item, toy-adjacent); and all furniture, kids, pet-supplies, bathroom fixtures/fittings, kitchen appliances/cookware/cutlery/bar-tools, textiles, and holiday-decoration categories per the standard exclusion rules - this is otherwise a very large general home/living catalogue (furniture, kids, pets, full kitchen) beyond just home decor, so only the qualifying decor/lighting/mirror/glassware/tableware branches were extracted.
